correctness.rationale: For finite N≥2, Ω,κ>0, show the no-jump generator has no imaginary-axis eigenmode by the boundary recurrence, hence the survival integral is the unique positive Hermitian solution of A†Q+QA=−I. Substitute the explicit parity-dependent kernel into all off-diagonal, diagonal, sink-boundary and terminal equations; affine index identities give exact equality. The mean follows from integrated survival, and strict convexity yields the site-dependent optimum. Checked actual standalone verify.py path using 4,960 exact rational matrix residuals and 90 independent spectral-integration tests. Limits: no general graph, no infinite path or arbitrary coherent-state common optimum; finite tests alone never prove general N.

originality.rationale: The mathematically specific novelty claim is the exact all-size parity-resolved integrated-survival Gramian for the finite open uniform quantum path with a single Lindblad sink, plus exact site-optimal absorption rates and far-end versus bulk lifetime scaling. The cited semi-infinite Lindblad model has different spectrum and nonunit total absorption; its primary conclusion explicitly calls finite geometries an open direction. The separate finite-chain unitary-defect source has no physical loss, and earlier Poisson projective monitoring uses a different quantum operation. Actual searches across first-passage, quantum transport and boundary-loss aliases found no stronger direct formula, but unindexed specialization of the general Lyapunov method remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A nonindexed earlier finite-chain dissipative-transport paper may already state the identical all-site lifetime or Gramian as a specialization of standard stable-Lyapunov theory.
The 2021 Entropy transport-efficiency review was not available in full at review time; its general transport formalism could reference a stronger earlier source.
Secondary and historical code-derived claims are not a substitute for an independent exhaustive priority review.

value.rationale: Finite reflecting geometry is specifically identified as outstanding in the 2026 exact semi-infinite Lindblad absorber source. The all-site closed-form integrated loss operator solves physically meaningful first-passage observables beyond total absorption probabilities and yields a nontrivial size-independent optimal loss rate for every site away from the sink, and a sharp linear far-end versus quadratic interior transport-time dichotomy. Those are experimentally interpretable geometry-dependent predictions, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a bare rewrite of the standard Lyapunov identity.
